questions.stem: What is the result of performing the Cartesian product between sets A = {1, 2} and B = {3, 4}? Write the pairs in the order (A element, B element).
questions.solution: The Cartesian product creates all possible combinations of elements from both sets without regard for their original order. The correct result is [(1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 4)].
questions.explanation: Each element from set A is paired with each element from set B.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to mix up the order of the elements or not include all possible pairs.

questions.stem: What is the result of performing the Cartesian product between sets A = {} and B = {5, 6}? Write the pairs in the order (A element, B element).
questions.solution: The Cartesian product of an empty set and any other set results in an empty set because there are no elements to pair with the elements from the non-empty set. The correct result is [].
questions.explanation: When one of the sets involved in the Cartesian product is empty, it does not contribute any elements to the resulting pairs.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to assume that an element from the non-empty set would be paired with the empty set, but this is not the case.

questions.stem: What is the result of performing the Cartesian product between sets A = {7} and B = {7}? Write the pairs in the order (A element, B element).
questions.solution: The Cartesian product of two sets with the same single element results in a set containing one pair. The correct result is [(7, 7)].
questions.explanation: Each element from set A is paired with each element from set B.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to think that there would be two pairs because of the repetition of the number 7, but in the Cartesian product, each element from set A is paired with each element from set B.

questions.stem: What is the result of performing the Cartesian product between sets A = {8, 9} and B = {8, 9, 10}? Write the pairs in the order (A element, B element).
questions.solution: Each element from set A is paired with each element from set B, regardless of whether the elements are repeated in either set. The correct result is [(8, 8), (8, 9), (8, 10), (9, 8), (9, 9), (9, 10)].
questions.explanation: Each element from set A is paired with each element from set B.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to overlook pairs where an element appears multiple times in one or both sets.

questions.stem: What is the size (number of elements) of the Cartesian product between sets A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {4, 5, 6}? Write the pairs in the order (A element, B element).
questions.solution: The size of the Cartesian product is equal to the product of the sizes of the two sets involved. In this case, |A| = 3 and |B| = 3, so |A × B| = 3 × 3 = 9.
questions.explanation: The number of elements in the Cartesian product is determined by multiplying the number of elements in each set together.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to confuse the size of the resulting set with the number of elements in one of the original sets.

questions.stem: What is the result of performing the Cartesian product between sets A = {1, 2} and B = {3, 4, 5}? Write the pairs in the order (A element, B element).
questions.solution: Each element from set A is paired with each element from set B. The correct result is [(1, 3), (1, 4), (1, 5), (2, 3), (2, 4), (2, 5)].
questions.explanation: Each element from set A is paired with each element from set B.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to overlook pairs where an element appears in one set but not the other.

questions.stem: What is the result of performing the Cartesian product between sets A = {a, b} and B = {c, d, e}? Write the pairs in the order (A element, B element).
questions.solution: Each element from set A is paired with each element from set B. The correct result is [(a, c), (a, d), (a, e), (b, c), (b, d), (b, e)].
questions.explanation: Each element from set A is paired with each element from set B.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to mix up the order of the elements or not include all possible pairs.
